HOW TO RESTORE FROZEN-SINGLE
==========================================================
You need exactly three ubiquitous open-source programs:
  par2  (github.com/Parchive/par2cmdline)  - repair
  gpg   (gnupg.org)                        - decrypt
  tar   (POSIX standard, preinstalled)     - extract
And the passphrase for key K-15F1461C (Obelisk keystore, or the
printed key card labelled K-15F1461C).

1) VERIFY / REPAIR (no passphrase needed):
     par2 verify FROZEN-SINGLE.tar.gpg.par2
     par2 repair FROZEN-SINGLE.tar.gpg.par2      (only if verify fails)
2) DECRYPT (prompts for passphrase):
     gpg -d -o FROZEN-SINGLE.tar FROZEN-SINGLE.tar.gpg
3) EXTRACT all, or one file:
     tar -xf FROZEN-SINGLE.tar
     tar -xf FROZEN-SINGLE.tar path/to/one/file

Integrity (SHA256):  ciphertext 4e64b34eaf71346d68ccfe4ea2437d95461d2d77d62c6e323b5eb14c70f40911   tar 4d5645094413d623561cd0849b85de876ed5925736a405c90279389bf19763dc
Full file list: FROZEN-SINGLE.manifest.json.gpg (encrypted; see PRIVACY below)
No compression anywhere — extracted bytes are the originals.
==========================================================

WINDOWS — the tar built into Windows writes each file name in the system's
code page. A name that code page cannot hold (Japanese on a Western system,
for example) is refused with "unreadable filename", and the other files are
restored. The package keeps every name as UTF-8: to restore those files too,
extract FROZEN-SINGLE.tar with a tar that keeps Unicode names, such as 7-Zip
(7z x FROZEN-SINGLE.tar).

PRIVACY — this medium's file listing is ENCRYPTED (FROZEN-SINGLE.manifest.json.gpg),
so a lost tape reveals no filenames. To read it:
     gpg -d FROZEN-SINGLE.manifest.json.gpg      (passphrase for key K-15F1461C)
